inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL migration adds a column conditionally and backfills it from a legacy column with a NULL guard.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Minimized to one incident row, one legacy column, one ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, one repeated idempotent DDL statement, and one guarded backfill.

fixture_notes: The new process_kind column is added twice without changing the table, then receives the legacy kind only when it is NULL.
determinism_notes: One fixed row and one ordered final read isolate conditional column creation and guarded backfill; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE incident_class_min (incident_id INT PRIMARY KEY, legacy_kind VARCHAR(16) NULL)

steps.sql: ALTER TABLE incident_class_min ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS process_kind VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT NULL
ALTER TABLE incident_class_min ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS process_kind VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT NULL
UPDATE incident_class_min SET process_kind = legacy_kind WHERE process_kind IS NULL AND legacy_kind IS NOT NULL
SELECT incident_id, legacy_kind, process_kind FROM incident_class_min ORDER BY incident_id

checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS process_kind_rows FROM incident_class_min WHERE process_kind IS NOT NULL
